calibration_targets.early_fraction_kind: ASSUMPTION (not fitted; AACT lacks per-event timing)

provenance.aact_source: real hosted AACT snapshot (data/clean/ref_*.parquet); build-time only
provenance.note: Real marginal/overall/reason-mix/sign targets are EDA values (not re-extracted). early_fraction is an ASSUMPTION (AACT has no per-event timing).
provenance.source: captured real EDA over validated ref_* tables

disclaimer: SYNTHETIC — calibrated to aggregate AACT statistics, NOT real participants, method-validity only, no PHI.
generation_note: Each real trial contributes an equal number of participants whose dropper fraction equals that trial's real participant-weighted rate, so the cohort reproduces the real TRIAL-MEAN marginal targets.

labelled_assumptions.age_years: Sampled within trial [min_age, max_age] when present, else 18-75.
labelled_assumptions.baseline_severity: Standardised 0-100 score; drawn per phase (later phase -> broader severity). Calibrated to published trial demographics, not AACT.
labelled_assumptions.comorbidity_count: Poisson count scaled by therapeutic area; synthetic.
labelled_assumptions.early_fraction: ASSUMPTION (not fitted): assumed share of dropout in the first half of planned duration. AACT aggregates lack per-event timing, so this is set by assumption (0.6), not estimated from data. See the early_fraction TODO in targets.py.
labelled_assumptions.per_trial_dropout_rate: Each real trial's dropper fraction equals its real participant-weighted rate (not_completed/started over its arms). With equal participants per trial, the cohort reproduces the real TRIAL-MEAN marginal dropout targets (phase, therapeutic_area, sponsor_class, blinding, site-count) and the real trial-mean overall.
labelled_assumptions.prior_trial_experience: Poisson count; synthetic, no AACT source.
labelled_assumptions.socioeconomic_proxy: Labelled synthetic 0-1 proxy; no real SES data exists in AACT.
labelled_assumptions.travel_friction: 0-1 proxy derived from trial n_sites (multi-site -> lower friction). Synthetic.
